security_audit.summary: Markdown backtick and placeholder URL detections are mostly formatting or example noise, but the traversal, sensitive-file, and command-execution findings are confirmed. The skill provides an offensive workflow for extracting sensitive files, automating traversal tests, and escalating LFI to command execution, so it is not suitable for unrestricted marketplace publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove payloads and target lists for system password files, SSH keys, SAM hives, and process environment files. Replace them with lab-only mock filenames and impact descriptions.
Remove command execution payloads, log poisoning steps, wrapper execution examples, and shell command validation. Keep only high-level risk explanation and defensive detection guidance.
Restrict fuzzing content to controlled labs with synthetic targets, rate limits, authorization checks, and explicit stop conditions.
Lead with secure design, code review, validation tests, and remediation workflows. Move any exploit discussion behind strict lab-only context.

content.value_statement: Unvalidated file path input can expose sensitive server files. This skill guides authorized testers through traversal validation, impact documentation, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Identifies file-handling parameters that may accept unsafe paths.
Explains Linux and Windows traversal validation concepts for authorized tests.
Outlines browser, proxy, cURL, ffuf, and wfuzz based testing workflows.
Documents encoding and filter-bypass concepts used during controlled assessment.
Connects discovered file exposure to impact analysis and remediation advice.
Provides secure coding guidance for canonical path checks and allowlists.
limitations: It is only appropriate for authorized systems and controlled training labs.
It cannot bypass operating system permissions or application access controls by itself.
The examples are generic and require careful scope and safety review.
It does not replace legal approval, written rules of engagement, or secure test data.

use_cases.title: Validate Download Endpoints
use_cases.description: Assess whether approved download or document-viewer routes expose files outside the intended directory.

use_cases.title: Review File Access Code
use_cases.description: Map risky path handling patterns to safer canonicalization, allowlist, and storage design recommendations.

use_cases.title: Teach Traversal Risk Safely
use_cases.description: Structure a lab session that shows traversal impact without touching production systems or real secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Review A File Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized file download feature for path traversal risk. Identify likely weak points and safe remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Scoped Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a path traversal test plan for my staging application. Include scope boundaries, evidence handling, and rollback criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me assess the impact of an authorized traversal finding. Focus on exposed file classes, severity, and stakeholder-ready wording.

prompt_templates.title: Design Safer Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure file access pattern for this service. Include canonical path validation, allowlists, storage isolation, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Assess an approved report download endpoint in staging.
output: A scoped test plan with target routes, allowed evidence, and stop conditions.
A severity rationale based on whether sensitive files are reachable.
A remediation checklist for allowlists, canonical paths, and least privilege.

output_examples.input: Explain a confirmed traversal finding to developers.
output: A concise impact statement for file exposure risk.
A developer-focused explanation of unsafe path joining.
A prioritized fix plan with validation and regression testing guidance.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe training lab for traversal testing.
output: A lab outline using mock files and isolated infrastructure.
Rules for avoiding real credentials and production data.
Discussion questions about secure design and monitoring.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, and allowed evidence before testing.
Use synthetic files or lab data whenever possible to avoid collecting real secrets.
Pair each validation result with concrete remediation and regression tests.
anti_patterns: Testing production systems without explicit written permission and agreed limits.
Collecting or storing credentials when a safer proof of exposure is enough.
Reporting payload success without explaining root cause and durable fixes.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for general use?
faq.answer: No. It contains offensive testing workflows and should only be used with explicit authorization.

faq.question: Can it be used for defensive code review?
faq.answer: Yes, when focused on finding unsafe path handling and planning secure remediation.

faq.question: Does it execute tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples, but users control any testing activity.

faq.question: What evidence should testers collect?
faq.answer: Collect the minimum proof needed, preferably from synthetic files or approved non-sensitive data.

faq.question: What are the main fixes?
faq.answer: Use allowlists, canonical path validation, storage isolation, and least-privilege file permissions.

faq.question: Which tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It references browser developer tools, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, cURL, ffuf, and wfuzz.
